subject.title: Feature: Floating agent bubbles (Clawi) for macOS

question: Should OpenClaw ship persistent per-agent floating desktop bubbles in the bundled macOS app, or first design a supported native UI/window extension seam for an external companion?
rationale: Existing code makes either direction conceivable but does not establish persistent per-agent windows as a product contract; the choice affects bundled app scope, native window behavior, state ownership, and chat routing.

options.title: Ship native bubbles
options.body: Implement a focused bundled macOS feature using canonical activity and session state, app-owned placement, accessibility-safe windows, and existing chat routing.

options.title: Design an extension seam
options.body: Add a reusable native activity, window, and chat-routing API before an external companion or plugin owns the bubble UX.

options.title: Keep current desktop UX
options.body: Decline persistent bubbles and retain the menu-bar HUD, session menu, and WebChat as the supported macOS interaction model.

recommendation.title: Ship native bubbles
recommendation.body: Implement a focused bundled macOS feature using canonical activity and session state, app-owned placement, accessibility-safe windows, and existing chat routing.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and strongest adjacent native macOS overlay, activity, and chat history point to this person as the best available decision owner.
